title: Unpack siblings and parents from family_members
description:
Unpack siblings and parents from family_members.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as unpack_family_members(family_members), where family_members is a tuple whose last two items are the father and mother and every earlier item is a sibling, returning a tuple (siblings_tuple, (father, mother)).
hints: Tuple unpacking lets you pull items into separate names in one assignment, and a starred name can soak up 'everything else' as a list.
The last two items of family_members are always the parents; whatever comes before them are the siblings.
Use *siblings, father, mother = family_members, then return (tuple(siblings), (father, mother)).
expected_behavior: Returns a 2-tuple: the siblings as a tuple, and (father, mother) as a tuple.
explanation: The starred assignment *siblings, father, mother = family_members assigns the last two items to father and mother and collects the remaining leading items into the siblings list, which is then converted back to a tuple.
